clue.text: Whip Australian into court

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: CT is the standard abbreviation for court
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian is dragged into court over a flogging.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside CT. The cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, the old naval flogging whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a knotted multi-thonged lash, once used for flogging sailors and prisoners.

clue.text: Funny to arrive and risk missing end of game

parts.note: to arrive is to come

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: to dice with death is to risk it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of game

explanation.surface: Someone turns up and gambles, leaving before the game finishes, which is comical.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, 'dice' means to take chances, as in 'dicing with death'; 'end of game' names the single letter to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic describes anything relating to comedy, so it serves as a synonym for amusing or humorous.

clue.text: Tense description of midnight activity of bird-watchers

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
midnight is called the witching hour

explanation.surface: A nervous account of what keen birders get up to at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective (nervous), but it is the grammar abbreviation T. Midnight is traditionally 'the witching hour'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, twitching is the hobby of chasing rare bird sightings, and its enthusiasts are called twitchers.

clue.text: Old man to understand about rupees and francs

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the others

parts.note: to gather is to understand, as in 'I gather'
R is the abbreviation for rupees
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for francs

explanation.surface: An elderly man tries to get his head round rupees and francs.
explanation.walkthrough: RANDF sits inside GATHER, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Old man' is informal for a father, and by extension an elderly relative; a grandfather is an elderly male forebear.

clue.text: Wind, Eastern, expressing a sort of air

indicators.note: to express is literally to press out, so a letter is squeezed out of the word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
the letter taken as written, to be removed
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A wind from the east carries a kind of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: GALE squeezes out its A, leaving GLE, then E is added. The 'a' of 'a sort of air' does double work as the letter lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied English part-song for three or more voices, so a kind of tune or melody.

clue.text: Takes responsibility for posters put around Cambridge University

indicators.note: placing one thing around another encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: posters are advertisements
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to putting posters up all over Cambridge University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge University' tempts a British solver to think of the English one; it is MIT, in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a fault is to confess it and accept blame, so owning up to a deed.

clue.text: Dada-inspired movement of French — this is just loony at the outset

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' (plural)

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only each word's opening letter is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An art movement inspired by Dada, which the French call simply mad from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word needed is the plural DES, not DE; the split into the enumeration's 2,5 comes only after the pieces join.
explanation.definitionFit: De Stijl was the Dutch abstract art movement of Mondrian and van Doesburg, which drew on Dadaist ideas.

clue.text: Attracted by wife-swapping? Naughtily aroused — and ultimately participating!

indicators.note: doing something naughtily is misbehaving, so the letters are put out of order
taking part means joining in, so these letters join the mix too

parts.note: taken as written
ult. is the dictionary abbreviation for ultimately

explanation.surface: A saucy account of swinging: getting excited, and in the end joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation ULT (as in 'ult.') is added to the letters of 'aroused' before the mix. The question mark flags the definition as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: Wife-swapping involves sex outside marriage, and anyone drawn to it is inclined to marital infidelity.

clue.text: Monster — English writer almost entirely upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, and almost entirely means all but a small part is turned

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist and poet

explanation.surface: A monstrous English writer who is nearly completely overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter stays put: H, then ARDY turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth slain by Heracles as one of his labours.

clue.text: Poorly earthed — rather high temperature

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so the letters come out in a faulty order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A badly grounded appliance runs rather hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at electrical wiring; the definition is literal, and understated with 'rather'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red heat is the temperature at which metal glows red, several hundred degrees, which is indeed fairly hot.

clue.text: A choice of ways forward when bringing in one crop

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a maze offers a choice of paths at every junction
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A farmer weighing options when harvesting one crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A choice of ways forward' is a cryptic description, not a word to find; 'bringing in' also suggests harvesting, the surface's disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, also called corn, is a cereal grain widely grown in fields for food and fodder.

clue.text: Ill-advised mug died horribly, touring island

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece travels around another
something done horribly is done badly, so the letters come out in a garbled order

parts.note: taken as written
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A foolish victim died horribly while touring an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters MGUIDED go round IS after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Misguided choices rest on bad judgement or poor advice, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with love

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to avoid or dodge
second meaning: an affectionate term of address, common in the north and Midlands of England

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a vow to shun romance. 'Duck' as a term of endearment is regional British, like 'love' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for evading something and a friendly English form of address like 'dear'.

clue.text: Burlesque act — parties set to be enlivened

indicators.note: livening something up changes it, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A burlesque performer is booked to liven up the parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is two whole words; the surface's parties are exactly where such an act might appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlesque shows traditionally featured comic turns and a performer slowly undressing to music.

clue.text: Italian painter floundering amid oil and gin

indicators.note: floundering is struggling clumsily, so the letters flail into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian artist struggling with his oil paint and his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amid' looks like a container signal but is part of the fodder; 'and' is the only word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian artist in Paris, famous for elongated portraits and nudes.

clue.text: Against fastening on edge, like some earrings?

indicators.note: fastening onto something grips it all round, so one piece holds another

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Someone objects to earrings that fasten on the edge of the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' as a con comes from 'pros and cons'. The question mark signals that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip-on earrings grip the earlobe with a spring clasp rather than passing through a pierced hole.

clue.text: Wind-player popular when in drink

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A wind musician is well liked once he has had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind-player' is the instrument that plays wind, not a musician; claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestras name players by instrument, and the clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument, blown to make music.

clue.text: Attachment to airship — concern with end dropping off

indicators.note: an end dropping off is lost, so the final letter is cut away

parts.note: care is concern or worry

explanation.surface: Worry that a part of an airship might fall off.
explanation.walkthrough: CARE loses its last letter. The dash separates definition from wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The passenger or crew compartment slung beneath an airship or balloon is known technically as its car, or gondola.

clue.text: Obligatory rise in desire, receiving moving caress

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards
to receive is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

indicators.note: something moving shifts position, so the letters rearrange themselves

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mandatory surge in longing as someone is stroked.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' turns the desire upside down, and the stroke's letters are then slipped between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something required or compulsory, which cannot be avoided or left out.

clue.text: Good quantity of wine in pub for wind-player

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a bar is a pub
G is the abbreviation for good
a pipe is a large wine cask, about 105 gallons

explanation.surface: A generous serving of wine at the pub for the musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good quantity' looks like one phrase meaning 'a lot'; it splits into G and a quantity of wine, a PIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpiper blows air into a bag to sound the pipes, so is a musician on a wind instrument.

clue.text: Wind-player's a fool, opening gift

indicators.note: one thing opening another splits it apart and sits in the gap

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or gift
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A wind musician is an idiot as he unwraps a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind-player’s' is read as 'wind-player is'; 'opening' makes the fool split the gift after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a large double-reed woodwind instrument, the bass of the orchestra's reed section.

clue.text: Resonant house in city in Gabon

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
HO is the abbreviation for house
taken as written
G is Gabon's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: An echoey building in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House in city' invites a container, but the pieces are laid end to end. 'The City' is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant space rings and reverberates, so sounds come back as repeated reflections.

clue.text: Drinks almost all of pitcher and gets cold

indicators.note: almost all falls short of the whole, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a pitcher is a jug
something that ices freezes, getting cold

explanation.surface: Someone downs most of a jug and catches a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' looks like a verb in the surface; it is the definition, a plural noun. JUG loses its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit juices are common soft beverages, so the plural noun matches 'drinks' exactly.

clue.text: Police operations involving Republican? They're pulled by those in power

definitions.text: They're pulled by those in power

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: stings are undercover police traps
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Covert police operations involving a Republican politician, with the powerful manipulating things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint to the idiom 'pull strings', to use influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling strings means using influence behind the scenes, something the powerful and well connected can do.

clue.text: Garden feature? Regard common garden shrub being trimmed

indicators.note: trimming clips off the tip, so the final letter is cut away

parts.note: to gaze is to look at, to regard
box is a common hedging shrub

explanation.surface: Looking at a garden where a common hedge is being clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garden feature?' looks like a cryptic signal for the whole clue but is just the definition; BOX loses its X.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small roofed pavilion in a garden, often with open sides, for sitting and admiring the view.

clue.text: Gloomy cellar — push for redecoration

indicators.note: redecorating rearranges a room, so the letters are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dingy basement, and someone pressing to have it done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloomy' looks like an adjective for the cellar, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepulchral means tomb-like, so dismal and funereal in mood or appearance, as in a sepulchral voice.

clue.text: Early religious leader's time imprisoned by Lord

indicators.note: being imprisoned by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a peer is a lord
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An early church leader serves time in jail at a Lord's command.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'is'. 'Lord' looks like God here, but it is a British peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter was chief of the apostles and is regarded as the first pope of the early Church.

clue.text: University series providing enjoyment of right

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
SER is the abbreviation for series

explanation.surface: A university lecture series that gives people the pleasure of certain rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses a legal sense that most solvers will not expect.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, user means the continued exercise of a right, such as a right of way established by long use.

clue.text: Tramps uncovered organ stop

indicators.note: taking the cover off strips the outside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: hoboes are tramps, American vagrants

explanation.surface: Homeless men without shelter halt at an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: HOBOES loses H and S. 'Organ stop' reads as a verb phrase but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe organs have reed stops named after orchestral instruments whose tone they imitate, and the oboe is one.

clue.text: Cut off very large signal? Is blocking that

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: to block a thing is to sit in its way, so one piece lodges inside the word just named

parts.note: a trace is a sign or indication
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cuts off a huge signal because something is jamming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' points back to the signal, so the insertion happens inside that word alone, before the outsize letters go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise someone is to exclude them from society or a group, cutting them off socially.

clue.text: Most of border invaded by American intelligence

indicators.note: something invaded has an intruder inside it, so one piece goes within the other
most falls short of all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a brink is an edge or border
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A frontier region is overrun by American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spying in the surface, but it means cleverness. BRINK loses its K, then A goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain is used to mean mental ability or cleverness, as in 'she has a good brain'.

clue.text: Carol's husband among our men treated in hospice

indicators.note: being among others means being surrounded by them, so one piece goes inside
things treated are processed and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to carol is to sing
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Carol's husband is one of our men being cared for in a hospice.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb to sing. SINGH goes inside the shuffled NUROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice cares for the dying, and a nursing home similarly offers residential medical care, so the two overlap.

clue.text: Detectives heading off? Agreed

indicators.note: the head is the front, so taking it off drops the first letter

parts.note: private eyes are detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives agree to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as departing, but it means losing the first letter: EYES without E.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Agreed!' and 'Yes!' are both interjections expressing consent or assent to a proposal.
